*Matter and antimatter should have cancelled each other into pure light at the Big Bang. A new paper says the thing that stopped it is a particle physicists wrote off for decades.*

Rishav Roshan at the University of Southampton and Sudipta Show at IIT Kanpur just published in *Physical Review Letters* that a decoupled *heavy neutrino* decayed so slowly it briefly dominated the energy of the entire early universe. That window moved the switch that decided how much matter survived.

What you'll learn:
✅ Why the *matter-antimatter* asymmetry is the biggest open question in physics
✅ How a particle too *weak* to matter ended up running the early universe
✅ The gravitational-wave fingerprint that could prove or kill the idea
